bachelor planning

Online bachelor’s completion: general studies or an aligned major

Compare a broad completion degree with an aligned major after SNHU evaluates your learning. A regular course calendar can suit students who prefer scheduled instruction and feedback.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Transfer evaluation
  • Broad elective placement where allowed
  • Scheduled online terms

What needs to be confirmed

  • Choose the exact degree before treating accepted credit as applied credit.
  • Major requirements, prerequisites and course offerings affect the finish schedule.
  • This profile contains no course-by-course SNHU map.
  • The existing library supplies this primary reference. Numeric limits were not independently rechecked for this guide.

Eligibility and your situation

  • Confirm the active award and your admission/location eligibility.
  • Ask how older, technical or nontraditional learning fits the degree.

A practical sequence

  1. Select exact degree and catalog.
  2. Submit every prior-learning record for official evaluation.
  3. Build the GE/major/elective/residency ledger.
  4. Approve any additional external learning before purchase.
  5. Schedule remaining SNHU courses by actual prerequisites and term offerings.
  6. Complete coursework, final audit and graduation.

Your next useful actions

  • Request evaluations for a broad degree and your preferred major.
  • Compare remaining courses rather than headline transfer percentages.
  • Obtain current prices and a term-by-term finish schedule.

associate planning

Online associate completion: exact award to confirm

A shorter credential family to compare with direct bachelor’s entry. Check whether the associate meets your purpose or adds useful value after its extra courses, charges and conferral time.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Associate milestone
  • Prior-credit evaluation
  • Associate-to-bachelor comparison

What needs to be confirmed

  • Choose an active award and exact catalog.
  • An intermediate credential can add cost or delay.
  • Associate transfer and institutional requirements need their own evaluation.

Eligibility and your situation

  • Confirm current availability and admission.
  • If planning a bachelor’s, ask how every associate course applies there.

A practical sequence

  1. Define whether the associate meets the actual requirement.
  2. Select award and obtain evaluation of all prior learning.
  3. Map GE, subject, elective and institutional blocks.
  4. Compare complete associate and direct-bachelor’s routes.
  5. Complete approved courses and submit records.
  6. Obtain final audit/conferral and any onward evaluation.

Your next useful actions

  • Request associate and relevant bachelor’s evaluations together.
  • Compare extra courses, fees and time for the credential.
  • Build the exact associate map before purchasing outside work.

Official & supporting sources

  • SNHU transfer admission and evaluation↗
  • SNHU associate transfer-credit explanation↗
Ask for an individual evaluation.

Credit limits, degree placement, institutional-credit requirements, and professional eligibility are separate decisions. Use the current catalog and get the receiving school’s written confirmation.
